clue.text: Girl plants kiss on six-footer's body

indicators.note: plants means sets down beside, so the kiss is placed next to the girl

parts.note: Thora is a girl's name
X is the conventional written kiss

explanation.surface: A girl gives a kiss to a tall man's torso.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-footer is an insect, with six legs, not a tall person; its middle body section is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's middle segment, bearing the legs, is called by this anatomical term.

clue.text: A deceiver raised about one half crown

indicators.note: about means going round, so the deceiver surrounds the one
in a down clue raised means the whole run is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or deceiver
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A liar lifts a coin worth half a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside RAT; with A in front that gives ARAIT, which 'raised' turns upwards. 'half crown' looks like the old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular headband is a partial crown worn by royalty or brides.

clue.text: Young animal doesn't start eating ground meat, as it's ground

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so one piece surrounds the other
the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a foal is a young horse

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters of meat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note: minced meat is eaten with something milled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' appears twice: first as the anagram signal on 'meat', then at the end as the definition, meaning milled.
explanation.definitionFit: This product is oats milled to a coarse powder, so it is a milled foodstuff.

clue.text: Thinking Greek noble, title not showing it

parts.note: aristo is short for aristocrat, a noble

indicators.note: not showing means the following word is removed from title

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek aristocrat thinks about a title he lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: TITLE without IT leaves TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The philosopher of ancient Athens, pupil of Plato, was a thinker from Greece.

clue.text: Dry rot is amusing? Not entirely a blast!

parts.note: fun means amusing

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a gust is a blast of wind

explanation.surface: Is a timber disease funny? Hardly a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: GUST cut short by 'Not entirely' gives GUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a decay of timber caused by a mould-like organism.

clue.text: Vessel about to be broken up

indicators.note: broken up means the word about is smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship is about to be wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ABOUT gives the German submarine.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine is a type of warship.

clue.text: Old vessel beginning to empty into measure of liquid

indicators.note: into means placed inside the measure

parts.note: a gallon is a unit for liquids

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of empty is taken

explanation.surface: An old ship starts to empty out liquid by the gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: The E from 'empty' goes inside GALLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A large sailing warship of the 16th century is a historic ship.

clue.text: Seedy nightspot where band on strike

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a strip is a narrow band
to club is to strike

explanation.surface: A disreputable venue where the musicians walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' and 'strike' suggest musicians on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment offering striptease is a sleazy late-night venue.

clue.text: Be unsuccessful catching insect as flycatcher

indicators.note: catching means holding inside

parts.note: to fail is to be unsuccessful
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bird fails to catch an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flycatcher' could be a spider or a plant, but here it is a bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan-tailed bird of Asia and Australasia belongs to the flycatcher family.

clue.text: Throw back fat, as stone impediment?

indicators.note: back means the word for throw is read backwards

parts.note: to lob is to throw
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: Throwing back lard like a stone barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: LOB backwards gives BOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stone or metal post blocks vehicles, so it is a stone obstruction.

clue.text: Plant, for example, worker planted in row

indicators.note: planted in means put inside the row

parts.note: a line is a row
an ant is a worker

explanation.surface: A gardener plants worker plants in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' at the start is the definition; 'planted in' is the container signal, an echo that hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet briar is a wild rose, a shrub.

clue.text: Sound produced with target exploding

indicators.note: exploding means the letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A noise made when a target blows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise; here it means solid, without flaws.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument has no holes, as does a sealed container.

clue.text: See every sherpa patting yaks heads

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Watch each mountain guide stroke his yaks on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or catch sight of something is to see it.

clue.text: Given little time, escaped back to Dutch town

indicators.note: back means the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
fled means escaped

explanation.surface: Given little time, someone fled back to the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: T with FLED makes TFLED, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the Netherlands is famed for blue-and-white pottery.

clue.text: Dog sees river round about end of path

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: about means the round goes around the letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of path is taken

explanation.surface: A dog sees a river, going round at the end of a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' is only a link joining definition and wordplay; the river is the one in Scotland and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A large rough-coated hound was bred for hunting stags.

clue.text: Difficult losing head completely without anger, in passionate manner

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter goes

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the anger is removed

parts.note: entirely means completely
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Losing heads, people behave passionately without anger.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD loses H to give ARD; ENTIRELY without IRE gives ENTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervently or with great zeal is how a passionate person acts.

clue.text: Course, single good man can't be trusted

parts.note: a dish is a course of a meal
one means single
St, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A single course served by a good man who cannot be trusted.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar or cheat is untrustworthy.

clue.text: Every one in match box

indicators.note: in means placed inside the match

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match
each means every one

explanation.surface: Everyone in the game gets a box.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; 'box' also hints at a cricketer's protective box, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden crate for shipping tea is a large box.

clue.text: Sword missed lad, but…

parts.note: to cut a class is to miss it
a lass is a lad but female, a girl

explanation.surface: A sword barely missed a boy, but...
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots invite the solver to finish the thought: a lad, but a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A short curved blade was carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Remove vegetation

explanation.definitionFit: To scrub something is to cancel or remove it; scrub is also low stunted vegetation.

clue.text: Defensive structure to attack a bit

parts.note: to ram is to attack by charging
a part is a bit

explanation.surface: A fortification to be attacked in part.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad wall or earthen bank protects a fort.

clue.text: Attempt to get photo

explanation.definitionFit: A go or try is a shot; a snapshot taken with a camera is also one.

clue.text: Crooked tycoon with firm agreement

indicators.note: crooked means bent, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest magnate makes a deal with a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' looks like a description of the tycoon; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Compliance or accord with rules is agreement.

clue.text: Singers start to improvise during short work

indicators.note: during means placed inside the other piece
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a chore is a piece of work

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of improvise is taken

explanation.surface: Singers begin to improvise during a brief piece.
explanation.walkthrough: CHORE cut short is CHOR; I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of vocalists, as in a church, is a body of singers.

clue.text: Hard to swallow? don't care!

explanation.definitionFit: Tough meat is chewy and hard to swallow; the exclamation 'Tough!' means too bad, I don't care.

clue.text: Are you all right about war? Then be disruptive

indicators.note: about means surrounding the war

parts.note: RU is text speak for are you
OK means all right
Nam is short for Vietnam, the war

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a friend is fine after a war, then rages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are you all right' is the text message 'R U OK'; 'Nam' is US slang for the Vietnam War.
explanation.definitionFit: To go berserk is to behave wildly and disruptively.

clue.text: Fat reversed, about to beat disease

indicators.note: about means going round the beat
reversed means the word for fat is read backwards

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
to tan is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: Fat backwards, about to defeat illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns the fat to give TEUS; 'beat' here means thrash, as in tanning a hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms.

clue.text: Walk out on sand

explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to walk out on them; an arid region of sand is also named so.

clue.text: Pain in side removed after wound heals?

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pain in the side when running is called this; a surgical suture is taken out once a cut heals.
